issues.body: TestDeployPathsAreRustInert claims to re-derive the deploy/ non-interference proof, and scripts/ci_select.py explicitly cites absence of include_str!/include_bytes!/path reads as part of that proof. However, test_deploy_tree_is_not_read_by_any_rust_ci_workflow only scans a hard-coded subset of workflow files. It never scans crate Rust sources, Cargo manifests/build scripts, or other build inputs for deploy/ references. A later include_str!("../../../deploy/...") (or equivalent build-script dependency) would make deploy changes affect the Rust artifact while this test stayed green and merge-group CodeQL/Rust lanes continued to skip.
issues.fix_hint: Add a fail-closed source/build-input audit for references or path escapes into deploy/ (covering Rust sources, build.rs, and Cargo manifests), or remove deploy/ from _ORCHESTRATION_SAFE until such an enforceable proof exists. The test should include a mutation/witness showing that introducing a representative crate-side deploy/ dependency makes the audit fail.
issues.title: Deploy inertness test does not verify crate/source references

verdict.summary: The merge-group gate is fail-safe at runtime and delegates classification appropriately, but the new deploy/ allowlist is justified by a test that does not actually re-derive its stated non-interference proof. The test checks only a fixed workflow-name list and never checks Rust/Cargo sources for compile-time or runtime consumption of deploy/. That leaves the allowlist able to become unsound while its claimed guard remains green.
